thought.text: Let me look at the complete process-compose root log from the very start of run 2 to see what happened at 23:46:18:

reasoning_content:
21 processes currently running (increased from 8). The seed has been executed (administrative-file-draft-seed finished with exit 0).

Still missing (terminated, no restart): document-management, formal-completeness, gesetze-normen-db, project-logic, temporal-job, examination, temporal-codec, feedback, identity-management, objections-management, rechtsaenderungs-monitoring, jura-db, gesetzesbegruendung-db (skipped), frontend (skipped).

Wait, "Completed: 12, Skipped: 5" — same as before. But the current RUNNING list includes administrative-file-draft, supplementary-requests, plausibility-notes — these were previously Completed but are now running (did a 2nd restart occur?). In fact, the previous list had administrative-file-draft as Completed; now it's RUNNING. So some of them did get restarted.

Hmm, wait, the previous status dump was before the 2nd restart wave. Current: 21 running. Previously 15. Improvement: project-logic? No — project-logic is not in the RUNNING list. What's running is: administrative-file-draft, agent-orchestration, comment, fpp, llm-client, plausibility-notes, protocol, supplementary-requests + 12 workers.

Still not running: project-logic, document-management, formal-completeness, examination, feedback, identity-management, objections-management, temporal-codec, temporal-job, gesetze-normen-db, gesetzesbegruendung-db (skipped), jura-db (skipped), frontend (skipped).

Key cascade: temporal-job was terminated → frontend will never run (dependency). project-logic terminated → project-logic-seed won't run → frontend won't run.

I need to restart these dead processes via the API: /process/restart/{name}. process-compose is currently healthy (hasn't been killed), so a restart via the API should work:
- project-logic (restart → then project-logic-seed? Seed status is "Skipped" — a restart might re-trigger it; or use /process/start/{name})
- document-management
- formal-completeness (→ formal-completeness-seed)
- gesetze-normen-db (→ jura-db, gesetzesbegruendung-db)
- temporal-job (→ frontend)
- examination, feedback, identity-management, objections-management, temporal-codec, rechtsaenderungs-monitoring (already terminated — but is it needed? Per the table it's not a dependency of the frontend. But it's part of the stack, so restart it)
- frontend: after dependencies become ready — use /process/start.

But wait — why did they exit with code 0 on this clean run?? "23:46:25 Exited exit_code=0 process=formal-completeness" — only about 4 seconds after start (processes started at 23:46:21)?! formal-completeness started around 23:46:18, exited with exit 0 at 23:46:25. That's very fast — before "Application startup complete"! And "was aborted" = process-compose sent a signal??

Ah, wait. I get it now!!! Look at the first entry: "23:46:18.225 Exited exit_code=-1 process=examination / Restarting examination in 3 second(s)... Restarts: 1". exit_code=-1 = killed by a signal. At 23:46:18 — that's when my first clean run started (process-compose started at around 23:46:18). Why would process-compose kill 8 processes (examination, document-management, temporal-job, feedback, identity-management, project-logic, supplementary-requests + probably more) 0.004 seconds after starting them?!

"Restarts: 1" — so they had already been restarted once?! But this is a fresh process-compose instance (I killed the old one, the log file was truncated by the new redirect >)...

Oh my god. I get it. The uvicorn processes from the first process-compose instance... no wait, I verified those are gone.

Hmm, wait — "Restarting ... Restarts: 1" at 23:46:18: process-compose counts restarts from its own state (fresh = 0). At startup it immediately recorded "Exited -1 ... Restarts: 1" — meaning each of these processes had started and exited with -1 within milliseconds of process-compose's startup.

exit_code=-1 = killed by a signal (128+... no, process-compose reports signals as negative numbers: -1 might be SIGHUP? Or -15=SIGTERM... convention: -15 = SIGTERM, -9 = SIGKILL, -1 = ?).

What sends a signal to a process right after fork? ... uv? No. A bash -c wrapper? No.

Ah, wait. I think I finally get it. **`uv run --locked`** — when process-compose starts `bash -c "uv run --locked --all-packages uvicorn ..."`, the first `uv run` might need to re-resolve or check the environment... no, that's not it.

Hmm, what about the **watchfiles reloader** (uvicorn --reload): the reloader watches files. If, at startup, uvicorn detects a file change (e.g., .env write, venv write, git, or process-compose's own file watching touching mtime), it restarts the server process — the server exits with... the reloader sends SIGTERM to the child and then restarts it. That would be a "Shutting down" log (a clean one!). But the uvicorn log should then show "Will watch..." / a new reloader. And the process shouldn't fully exit.

But "process=examination Exited exit_code=-1" = the top-level bash/uv process exited. Hmm.

Let me think about 23:46:18 more carefully. process-compose starts at 23:46:18 (per root log) (project start 23:46:18). The "Started command=..." lines are at 23:46:21 (3 seconds later = restart backoff!). So the timeline is:
- 23:46:18: processes started (batch 1)
- 23:46:18.225: examination, document-management, temporal-job, feedback, identity-management, project-logic, supplementary-requests (+ more) immediately "Exited exit_code=-1" → "Restarting in 3 second(s)"
- 23:46:21: batch 2 started
- 23:46:25-27: formal-completeness, rechtsaenderungs-monitoring, objections-management, temporal-codec "Exited exit_code=0" → "aborted and won't become ready" (exit 0 = success → no restart!)
- 23:46:49-54: administrative-file-draft-seed (0), feedback (0), gesetze-normen-db (0), examination (0), identity-management (0)
- 23:46:58: project-logic (0) → "aborted, won't become ready" → project-logic-seed won't run
- 23:46:59: temporal-job (0) → frontend won't run
- 23:47:00: document-management (0)

So the first batch of 7-8 processes was killed with a signal about 0.004 seconds after start?! Impossible as normal execution — unless the signal came during spawn. And the second batch (started at 23:46:21) was cleanly terminated with exit 0 several seconds later (formal-completeness at 23:46:25, 4 seconds after start).

Wait, wait. Actually, let me reconsider: exit_code=-1 might mean process-compose couldn't determine the code (process died during spawn). And the batch-1 "Exited" at 23:46:18.22x — 4ms after the first start... but when did batch 1 actually start? The first "Started command=" line I saw is 23:46:21. Maybe batch 1 started at 23:46:18.0 and exited at 23:46:18.2 — 0.2 seconds after start.

What kills 8 uvicorn processes 0.2 seconds after fork, and then also sends a clean SIGTERM to all the rest a few seconds later?

... A previous process-compose that's still alive? I killed PID 18011 at 23:44:20 (18011 is gone). But wait — what about the first instance (PID 18011)?... killed. The TUI-less one? There's only one.

Wait, let me actually re-verify: is another process-compose running? The pgrep from earlier (after teardown) was... I ran `pgrep -af "process-compose up"` at 23:44:55 → returned 17988, 18011, + self. Then I killed 18011 → 18011 and 17988 gone. OK, so as of 23:44, only one instance.

Hmm, and a subtle point: the new run's root log is a new file (23:46, 14965 bytes) — consistent with a fresh instance.

So within a single fresh process-compose instance: 8 processes spawned and killed by signal about 0.2 seconds later. The remaining 14 started at 23:46:21 (after the 3-second backoff), ran for 4-40 seconds, then received a clean SIGTERM (exit 0).

What if... process-compose has a per-process "start timeout" or "health" check that fails immediately and terminates the process? No such feature.

What if the processes' own stdout pipes are closed and the writes SIGPIPE?? No.

If it's the WSL kernel: killing... no, no OOM record.

Actually, wait. Let me look at the "Exited" messages more carefully — I might be misreading the order. The 23:46:18 "Exited" events might correspond to processes that started in a previous project run (the old instance at 23:31:41) — if the new process-compose loaded the old state! process-compose has `--keep-project` and state restoration... the new instance starts fresh; it doesn't restore other people's processes.

Hmm, but actually — the 23:46:18 "Exited exit_code=-1" + "Restarts: 1"... the new instance's "Restarting X in 3 second(s)" explains the "Started" batch at 23:46:21 for exactly those 8 processes (protocol, document-management, gesetze-normen-db, temporal-job, examination, project-logic, identity-management, feedback — from the "Started" list at 23:46:21!). YES! The "Started" commands at 23:46:21 are: 18016 (protocol), 18001 (document-management), 18020 (gesetze-normen-db), 18015 (temporal-job), 18009 (examination), 18000 (project-logic), 18013 (identity-management), 18011 (feedback). And the "Exited -1 / Restarting" at 23:46:18: examination, document-management, temporal-job, feedback, identity-management, project-logic, supplementary-requests... (supplementary is in the exited list but not in the 23:46:21 started list — hmm, close enough, maybe there's more).

So: at instance startup (23:46:18.0), about 8 processes started and exited with a signal about 0.2 seconds later. At 23:46:21 they were restarted. The others (started at 23:46:18, fpp, formal-completeness, etc.) survived the first wave but were cleanly terminated with exit 0 between 23:46:25 and 23:47:00.

Two different phenomena:
A) About 8 processes killed by a signal about 0.2 seconds after first start (batch 1a)
B) About 14 processes cleanly terminated (SIGTERM) 7-80 seconds after start

For B, the clean SIGTERMs in that 23:46:25-23:47:00 window... what event happened in that window? Let me check the docker infrastructure: did a container restart at 23:46:25?? If, say, the keycloak or postgres container crashed/restarted at that moment... but process-compose doesn't watch docker.

Hmm, or — the `nohup bash -c` wrapper: when my terminal command finished (each terminal invocation runs in a timeout wrapper and gets killed!), did the SIGHUP cascade to the background process?? The nohup'd process should be immune to SIGHUP. But `uv run` spawns a co-process... nohup protects the bash -c and the process-compose child (same session? nohup redirects and ignores SIGHUP for the process it launches).

But wait — the earlier first run (23:31:41) had the same pattern! The 23:32:17-23:33:32 window = when my `nohup` command's terminal session ended (the command "started" and returned; the timeout wrapper process exited about 45 seconds later). Hmm, in that case: the 23:32:14-23:32:48 terminations... my first process-compose command's output was displayed and the command "finished" — the wrapper killed the entire process group (timeout's --signal=TERM --kill-after=5s kills the wrapper's process group!). The nohup'd bash should ignore SIGHUP, but a process group TERM kill = SIGHUP is irrelevant — nohup only protects from SIGHUP, not SIGTERM!

That's it!!! The terminal wrapper runs: `timeout --signal=TERM --kill-after=5s 600s bash -c '...'`. When the foreground command (the nohup line that echoes the pid) finishes, the wrapper's bash exits, and timeout... hmm, actually the wrapper exits normally when the foreground command completes — no kill needed. The nohup'd background process keeps running. That's why process-compose survived for minutes.

Hmm, so no. But wait — the kill did happen at a specific moment... the 23:46:25-23:47:00 terminations — what was I running in the terminal at that time? I launched process-compose with a `nohup ... &; echo; sleep 15; tail` command. That command completed at about 23:46:33 (after sleep 15). Then my next command (120-second sleep + checks) started at about 23:46:40 and ran until about 23:48:40. The termination window 23:46:25-23:47:00 overlaps with the first command (23:46:18-23:46:33)!!

So: the first launch command's wrapper exited at 23:46:33 → something sent SIGTERM to the app processes between 23:46:25-23:46:33?? But the terminations continued until 23:47:00 (after the command ended at 23:46:33).

Hmm, no. Actually, wait: was the nohup'd background process in the wrapper's process group? `bash -lc 'set -o pipefail; cd /workspace; nohup bash -c "..." & echo pid; sleep 15; tail'` — the nohup'd process is a child of the wrapper's bash, in the same process group (no new pgrp). When the wrapper's bash finishes, the children are reparented to init — no signal.

But — uv run! `nohup bash -c 'uv run --locked poe process-compose ...'` — uv spawns process-compose... all in the same process group. No signal at exit.

OK, so let me look at what the first batch's (A) 0.2-second death + the second wave's (B) clean termination have in common. The simplest hypothesis that fits both: **something is sending a signal in bursts**: at 23:46:18.2 (wave 1: signal, exit -1) and at 23:46:25-23:47:00 (wave 2: SIGTERM, exit 0). And in run 1: the terminations at 23:32:14-23:33:32 (wave: SIGTERM, exit 0, after about 1-2 minutes from the 23:31:41 start).

Hmm, hmm. In run 1 the terminations started at 23:32:14 (33 seconds after start). In run 2 the terminations are at 23:46:25 (7 seconds) to 23:47:00 (42 seconds). In run 2, wave 1 was at 23:46:18 (0.2 seconds, signal).

What happens in my terminal session about 30-90 seconds after launch? Nothing in particular... the sleep-120 command started at about 23:46:40.

Hmm, what about the docker compose up --wait wrapper? It finished long ago. The LLM stub nohup? Running fine.

OK, another thought — **process-compose's own readiness probe + `restart: on_failure`**: no...

Let me stop hypothesizing from memory and look at the complete root log from the start of run 2 — the first 50 lines should tell me exactly what happened at 23:46:18.
